newsitem.title: USA: No takers, not even nudists, for Florida village.
newsitem.headline: No takers, not even nudists, for Florida village.

text.p: After two years on the market without a serious nibble, residents of Lazy Lakes are giving up an effort to sell their tiny village en masse, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel said Monday.

The broker who listed the property has had inquiries from a Kuwaiti prince, a Latin American pop singer and even O.J. Simpson, who had an associate phone but never came to see the village, the newspaper said.
But nobody has considered paying the $15 million asking price, which includes 13 homes, the town's main -- and only -- street and a 3-acre lake stocked with bass.

Resident Joseph Fodera, who claims credit for the idea of selling the village as a block, acknowledged all the homes could probably be bought individually for about $5 million. But he said there would be advantages to owning the whole village.

"You could do anything you want if you owned it. If you wanted to walk around nude inside there, you could just pass an ordinance and it would be legal, you wouldn't get hassled," Fodera told the Sun-Sentinel.

With no sales prospects on the horizon, only seven of the village's 13 homeowners voted to renew Lazy Lakes' contract with real estate broker Sue Carolyn Wise, which expires next month. Three residents have put their homes on the market individually, including Fodera.
